title: Computation of the encoded pair predicate
statement: For every finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the Boolean alphabet and all Boolean words $x$ and $u$, the pair-loader machine of $N$, started on the self-delimiting encoding of $(x,u)$ from its initial configuration, halts with output the one-bit word whose bit is $1$ exactly when the run of $N$ on $x$ under choice word $u$ halts with output $[1]$. It does so in exactly three times one more than the length of the encoded pair.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
replaced: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet and let $x$ and $u$ be binary strings. On the self-delimiting encoding of the pair $(x,u)$, the pair-loader machine of $N$ halts from blank tapes within $3(\ell + 1)$ steps, where $\ell$ is the length of the encoded pair, and outputs the single bit recording whether the run of $N$ on $x$ under choice word $u$ has halted with output the one-bit string $1$.
